signal.title: [docs] Lowercase "Ray dashboard" across the docs
signal.text: ## Why this change "Dashboard" is a generic noun, so it stays lowercase next to a product name for the same reason "autoscaler" does. That's the convention #65239 settles, on @win5923's reasoning in [this review comment](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/65239#issuecomment-5283520022). This PR applies it across the docs. Splitting it out from the rule change keeps each one reviewable on its own: #65239 is the rule and the tooling, this is the mechanical sweep, and the diff here is casing with no prose rewrites. Same split as #65423, which retires "Ray Pod." **This depends on #65239 landing first.** If the convention changes in that review, this sweep changes with it. ## Scope All of `doc/source`, `.md` and `.rst`. 215 replacements across 53 pages, in prose: body text, headings, front matter and `.. meta::` descriptions, a glossary term, table cells, image alt text, and link and cross-reference text. Three commits, each reviewable on its own: the Kubernetes pages, the same term across the rest of the docs, and then the bare "Dashboard" that the first two left behind. The first commit covers `cluster/kubernetes/`, which is where #65239 scopes its Vale ruleset. The second extends the same convention to the rest, so it holds on every surface rather than only where the tooling happens to point: `ray-observability/`, `serve/`, `ray-core/`, `train/`, `ray-security/`, `ray-overview/`, the non-Kubernetes `cluster/` pages, `data/`, `rllib/`, and `ray-references/`. Headings are included deliberately. This guide requires sentence case for every heading, so "## Step 5: Access the Ray Dashboard" was already a defect on two counts. **The `ray-observability/getting-started` page title changes**, from "Ray Dashboard" to "Ray dashboard." That's the canonical dashboard page, so it's the most visible line in the diff and worth a deliberate look. Cross-references to it that don't set their own text pick the new title up automatically. ## Applied by script, reviewed by hand The sweep ran from a fence-aware script rather than find-and-replace, because a blind pass would have hit literal blocks and rewritten CLI output. It tracks Markdown code fences, treats MyST directive fences such as ```` ```{admonition} ```` as the prose they contain, and tracks rST literal blocks introduced by both `.. code-block::` and a trailing `::`. I reviewed all 162 replacements and each of the 9 exclusions individually. ## Deliberately not changed **Nine uses inside literal blocks**, because the rule governs prose. Eight are shell comments, five of them `# Step 7: Check Ray Dashboard...` in `k8s-ecosystem/ingress.md`. The ninth is literal CLI output in `user-guides/kubectl-plugin.md` (`Ray Dashboard: http://localhost:8265`), where changing it would misreport what the command prints. That leaves a page or two with a lowercase heading above a capitalized shell comment. I'd rather flag that than quietly edit code blocks in a prose sweep. Happy to include the eight comments if a reviewer prefers consistency within the page. **One use in `cluster/kubernetes/configs/static-ray-cluster.tls.yaml`**, a comment in a sample manifest rather than a docs page. **Nothing, as it turns out.** An earlier revision of this description claimed 217 bare capitalized "Dashboard" uses were being left alone. That number was wrong: the command behind it piped `grep -o` output into a `grep -v` filter that could never match, so it counted every occurrence of the word including the ones inside "Ray Dashboard". The real figure was 93, and the third commit sweeps the 54 of those that are the generic noun. What stays capitalized is listed above. **`README.rst` and the `python/` docstrings.** Eight files outside `doc/` use the term, mostly in docstrings that render into the API reference. Different surface, different owners. ## Bare "Dashboard" The third commit covers the 54 uses of a bare capitalized "Dashboard" that the term sweep left behind, which otherwise put "the Dashboard" next to "the Ray dashboard" on the same page. Most are a pure case change. Fifteen needed an article, because the prose used the word as a bare proper noun: "expose Dashboard outside the Cluster" becomes "expose the dashboard outside the Cluster", and three sentences opening "Dashboard is..." become "The dashboard is...". The installation extras table is the one place where a bare lowercase "dashboard" would have read badly, sitting in a list of Ray library names ("Core, Dashboard, Cluster Launcher"). Those rows and the tip below them now say "Ray dashboard". Left capitalized, because these aren't the generic noun: - CloudWatch's Agent, Dashboard, and Alarm config files, plus Grafana's Dashboard and Default Dashboard. - The literal **Open Dashboard** button label in the History Server UI. - Title and label positions where any word would capitalize: the "Dashboard (Web UI)" section title, a `Dashboard` tab label, and a `**Dashboard**` list label. - Twelve uses inside literal blocks, one of which is dashboard log output. ## Six adjacent lines Lowercasing one word of an otherwise title-case heading reads as a botched edit, so where that happened the whole heading goes sentence case: - `cluster/configure-manage-dashboard.md`: "Configuring and Managing Ray Dashboard" to "Configuring and managing Ray dashboard," plus the two link texts and one `:ref:` text that mirror that page title. - `ray-observability/user-guides/profiling.md`: "Ray Dashboard View" to "Ray dashboard view." - `ray-core/internals/token-authentication.rst`: "Ray Dashboard Flow" to "Ray dashboard flow." One more of the same kind in the first commit: alt text in `user-guides/kuberay-dashboard.md` read "KubeRay dashboard List of RayJobs" after the swap, so "List" lowercases too. ## Known cosmetic wart `user-guides/kuberay-history-server.md:13` now reads "see [Ray dashboard](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-observability/getting-started.html)" against a target whose published title is still title case. This PR retitles that page, so the two converge once it lands. The sentence is redundant as written either way. ## Testing No code, no API, no behavior change. Most replacements are identical in length. The ones that aren't are the fifteen that gained an article and the installation table rows, so rST title underlines needed checking rather than assuming: one title, "Set up Dashboard" becoming "Set up the dashboard", grew past its underline and is fixed. Verified against `master` that the change introduces no other short underline anywhere in `doc/source`. Verified with Vale 3.12.0, running the ruleset from #65239 against this branch: the `Ray Dashboard` and `KubeRay Dashboard` swaps go from 44 alerts to **0** on the paths that ruleset scopes, and `doc/source/data/` holds at 170 with no new alerts. Vale doesn't cover the other paths in this PR, and it has no rule for the bare noun at all, so the rest was verified by hand against a categorized list of every occurrence. Verified by hand that nothing in the repo references any of the changed heading strings, so no cross-reference or link text goes stale. Nothing here is enforced in CI. The Vale pre-commit hook remains scoped to `doc/source/data/`. ## AI assistance Written with AI assistance (Claude). The script is mine, I've reviewed every replacement and exclusion individually, and I can defend the change end to end.

signal.title: [core] Export the cluster ID to node-spawned processes instead of fetching it from the GCS
signal.text: ## Why are these changes needed? Every process that connects to the GCS without a cluster ID issues a `NodeInfoGcsService.GetClusterId` RPC during `Connect()`. During mass cluster bring-up the GCS is busy with node registrations, those fetches time out, and `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` is fatal to the connecting process — we hit this as fleet-wide bring-up deaths at 400 nodes on Ray 2.56 (see #64845 / #64847 for the server- and client-side halves of that incident). The most effective fix is to not fetch a constant at scale: the node that spawns a process already knows the cluster ID. Workers, raylets, the dashboard, and both agents already receive it on their command line; this PR covers the remaining node-spawned processes **through the environment** (no new CLI flags), and fixes a latent bug that made two more paths fetch unnecessarily: 1. **Bug fix (`python/ray/includes/common.pxi`):** `GcsClientOptions.create` passed `allow_cluster_id_nil` twice to the C++ constructor, silently ignoring `fetch_cluster_id_if_nil`. Every caller requesting `fetch_cluster_id_if_nil=False` with a nil ID — `services._get_gcs_client_options` and `services.wait_for_node`, i.e. **every `ray start` on every node** — actually fetched. That is an O(nodes) unnecessary `GetClusterId` storm during exactly the bring-up window where the GCS is most backlogged. 2. **Env-based distribution:** the node exports `RAY_CLUSTER_ID` via `start_ray_process(env_updates=...)` when spawning the log monitor and the autoscaler monitor (v1 and v2), and Python `GcsClient` falls back to that variable when constructed without a cluster ID (`_raylet.pyx`). The spawned processes therefore need **zero code changes** — no argparse, no constructor plumbing — and any future process spawned with the variable set is covered for free. An unset variable (drivers, external tools, kuberay-launched monitors) keeps today's fetch-from-GCS fallback. Remaining fetchers after this PR (intentionally out of scope — not spawned by a node that knows the ID): drivers connecting via `ray.init(address=...)`, CLI tools (`ray status` etc.), and the ray client proxy. #64845/#64847 keep those robust. ## Related issue number None found — searched open PRs/issues for GetClusterId / cluster ID distribution before opening (companion PRs #64845, #64847 cover the same incident's server/client halves; no overlap in files or mechanism). Not a duplicate of in-flight work. ## Checks - [x] I've signed off every commit (DCO). - [x] I've run pre-commit on the changed files. - [x] Testing strategy: - New `python/ray/tests/test_cluster_id_distribution.py` asserts `start_log_monitor` / `start_monitor` (v1 and v2) pass `env_updates={"RAY_CLUSTER_ID": ...}` when given a cluster ID and omit it otherwise (registered in `python/ray/tests/BUILD.bazel`, small). - Verified the spawn-side assertions locally against a nightly-wheel venv (the `GcsClient` env fallback in `_raylet.pyx` requires a built wheel and is exercised in CI by every test that starts a cluster and a log monitor/monitor). - The `common.pxi` change is exercised by every CI test that calls `ray start`/`wait_for_node`; the C++ flag semantics (`ShouldFetchClusterId`) are already unit-tested. Per the repo's AI contribution policy: AI assistance was used to develop this change; every changed line was reviewed and the tests above were run locally.

signal.title: [core][metrics] Add PrometheusCollector: mirror any /metrics exposition into Ray metrics
signal.text: ## Description Adds `ray.util.prometheus_collector` (DeveloperAPI): mirrors every series from a Prometheus text exposition into Ray custom metrics via `MetricRegistry`, so external engines' metrics (SGLang, vLLM, TGI, node_exporter, ...) surface in Ray's Prometheus export with a `ray_` prefix. Names, types, labels, and HELP text are discovered from the exposition itself — nothing is hard-coded. The common case is two lines: ```python collector = PrometheusCollector("http://127.0.0.1:30000/metrics") collector.start() # scrape every 2s in a daemon thread; collector.stop() to end ``` The constructor accepts a URL string (wrapped in `HTTPSource` with `timeout_s`) or any `Source` (`fetch() -> str`) for tests/files, and builds a `MetricRegistry` from `namespace=` unless a pre-built one is injected (mutually exclusive). Translation semantics: - **Counters**: cumulative → per-scrape deltas, with correct reset handling — a value that goes backwards means the source restarted, so the new reading is recorded as the increment since zero rather than dropped. - **Histograms/summaries**: sub-series (`_bucket`/`_sum`/`_count`, quantiles) are gauge-mirrored with all labels intact; Ray's native `Histogram` needs raw `observe()` calls that pre-aggregated buckets can't provide. Declaration is per *sample* name so `le` and friends keep their tag keys. - `_created` series and NaN values are skipped by default; filters are pluggable. `scrape()` is pure w.r.t. the network for fixture-driven unit testing; the built-in `start()`/`stop()` loop is restartable (fresh stop event per run), stops promptly (interruptible wait), and retries scrape errors with exponential backoff, modeled on serve's metrics loops. This is PR 2 of a 3-PR stack (stacked on #64670; only the last commit is new here): 1. #64670 — `MetricRegistry` 2. **This PR** — `PrometheusCollector` 3. Migrate serve's `haproxy_metrics.py` onto the registry ## Related issues N/A ## Additional information ``` python -m pytest python/ray/tests/test_prometheus_collector.py # 15 passed ``` Covers per-scrape deltas, counter reset, `_total` name folding, histogram sub-series label preservation, filter injection, HELP/`:` sanitizing, late-label warn-and-drop, constructor conveniences (URL/timeout/namespace, registry-vs-namespace exclusivity), and start/stop/restart/error-survival of the scrape loop.

signal.title: [Data] [5/11] Add the Parquet FooterReader actor pool
signal.text:
## Why Footer IO for the footer-based Parquet chunking path (the rest of the split of #64985). Reading N Parquet footers serially on the driver doesn't scale — it's the step that decides which row groups a read even touches. `FooterReader` runs as a pool of Ray actors, each reading footers on its own thread pool and streaming results back in batches, so footer IO spreads across the cluster instead of bottlenecking on one process. **Nothing constructs it yet** — it's unused until the footer indexer lands in step 6. ## Flow Per file, it produces the row-group descriptors the bin packer (merged in #65210) consumes: ```mermaid flowchart LR B["(path, size) batch"] --> A["FooterReaderActor
SPREAD across the cluster"] A --> R[read footer] R --> F["split_by_row_group(filter)
prune by statistics"] F --> Q["split_by_row_group(~filter)
classify fully_matched"] Q --> C["coalesce_row_groups
(from #65210)"] C --> O["stream List[FileChunks]
batched by result_batch_size"] ``` Three things it decides, each of which the packer and the limit push-down depend on: - **Predicate pruning.** `fragment.split_by_row_group(filter)` drops row groups whose Parquet statistics contradict the pushed filter, so they never reach the packer at all. - **`fully_matched` classification.** A surviving group is *fully* matched iff `~filter` prunes it entirely. Only fully-matched groups have an exact survivor count, and only exact counts may drive limit push-down. Any failure defaults to not-fully-matched, which is always the safe direction. **This is the correctness-critical bit**: nulls are the interesting case, since Parquet min/max stats are computed over non-null values only, so a group whose non-null values all satisfy the filter looks fully matched by bounds alone while its null rows don't survive. - **Projection-scoped sizing.** Byte sizes are accounted over only the projected leaf columns, so bins get sized for what the reader will actually fetch. Nested columns expand to all their leaves. ## What changed Two new files, 368 insertions, 0 deletions: | File | Change | | --- | --- | | `listing/footer_reader.py` | **new** — `FooterReader` plus `FooterReaderActor = ray.remote(FooterReader)`. Kept as a plain class with the actor built via the functional form, so callers can type handles as `ActorProxy[FooterReader]`. `read_footers` is a streaming `@ray.method` generator that yields `List[FileChunks]`, batched by `result_batch_size` — the driver pays one object-store fetch per yielded list, so batching cuts driver-side deserialization roughly proportionally. | | `tests/test_footer_reader.py` | **new** — 14 tests | ## Testing The tests drive the plain class directly against local Parquet fixtures — no actor, no cluster. Coverage is aimed at the decisions above rather than the plumbing: predicate pruning by statistics, the partial-match case (`id >= 30` splitting a row group, which must **not** count as exact), a predicate matching nothing, projection shrinking accounted size while leaving row counts alone, coalescing preserving total rows, nested columns expanding to all leaves, and result batching at several `result_batch_size` values. ``` $ python -m pytest -q python/ray/data/_internal/datasource_v2/tests/test_footer_reader.py 14 passed in 4.30s $ python -m pytest -q python/ray/data/_internal/datasource_v2/tests/ python/ray/data/tests/unit/datasource_v2/ 145 passed in 0.90s ``` ## Stack Step 5 of an 11-step split of #64985, which was 43 files / +3234 −719 and not reviewable as one unit. - #65167 `[1/11]` Extract `FileIndexer.list_file_infos` ✅ merged - #65168 `[2/11]` Push limit into `ReadFiles` when `Limit` sits directly on it ✅ merged - #65214 `[3/11]` Derive `ListFiles` pushdown state from the scanner ✅ merged - #65210 `[4/11]` Parquet footer types + online bin packer ✅ merged - **this PR** `[5/11]` — depends on #65210 for `parquet_footer_types` and `parquet_row_group_coalescing` - #65169 `[9/11]` Pin the Parquet footer actor pool to 1 in tests (open, independent) Step 6 wires this and the packer together behind an opt-in flag, and needs both this and #65214. --- Not a duplicate of any open PR (checked `gh pr list --state open` plus a file-level overlap check against #65142 / #63158 / #64404 — no overlap; only #64985, which this replaces). Upon init, ShuffleFileServer will bind file serving function to a random available port. - Fault tolerance is driven by Ray's actor state (ActorDied / ActorUnavailable / ActorUnschedulable). On mid-fetch TCP failure, the reducer compares endpoints: if the manager was restarted (where the endpoint are likely to be different) we retry in place; if the endpoint is unchanged (which is Ray RPC still works but our TCP path doesn't) it's almost always a network-configuration problem (NetworkPolicy, firewall, routing) that retries to the same manager can't fix, so we surface a terminal ShuffleFileServerAnomalyError. ## Additional information The complete implementation of shuffle is in https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/64733, including runtime libraries, external shuffle task definition, plan wiring and a user-visible flag. signal.title: [Data][LLM] Add multi-host TPU batch inference for Ray Data LLM
signal.text: ## Summary I wrote a design document for this feature [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1E6wd-WWl6ahtTd95ngsMBc1UmoYXsvFFm__Nu_ueryk/edit?tab=t.0). This PR adds multi-host TPU support to Ray Data LLM batch inference (`vLLMEngineProcessorConfig` / `build_processor`). With a TPU `accelerator_type` and a topology in `accelerator_config`, each engine actor reserves its own TPU slice placement group and runs on bundle 0 (CPU only, `capture_child_tasks=True`), so the engine's vLLM workers are gang-scheduled onto the slice. Accelerator config/backends live in `python/ray/llm/_internal/common/accelerators.py` and are shared with Serve. Batch scheduling now resolves through `AcceleratorBackend.build_batch_scheduling_options`, so the builder calls the backend unconditionally and `vLLMEngineStage.post_init` is removed. The GPU path keeps its existing behavior (same bundles, same PACK placement group per actor), just built in `GPUAccelerator` instead of the stage. ```python config = vLLMEngineProcessorConfig( model_source="...", accelerator_type="TPU-V6E", accelerator_config={"kind": "tpu", "topology": "4x4"}, # TP * PP * DP must equal topology chip count (PP/DP default to 1). engine_kwargs={"tensor_parallel_size": 16}, ) processor = build_processor(config) out = processor(ds) ``` Both backends build their scheduling strategy in a static `_scheduling_strategy_fn` passed to `ray_remote_args_fn` via `partial`, so Ray Data invokes it once per actor replica. `concurrency > 1` works on TPU: each replica gets its own slice. `chips_per_vm` field is also added for the TPU backend to support ambiguous topologies (v6e `2x4`, etc.). This field is already accepted by `SlicePlacementGroup` so I just added it to the parameters users can specify for TPU in their config. ## Behavior changes - `accelerator_type="CPU"` is rejected for vLLM batch inference - `get_accelerator_backend` raises on unrecognized configs - TPU fill constraint is `tensor_parallel_size * pipeline_parallel_size * data_parallel_size == topology chips` (PP/DP default to 1). This diverges from GPU (`tp*pp` only) because the TPU slice size is fixed by topology and equality must count every device dimension. - TPU slice bundles carry `accelerator_type:<TYPE>: 0.001`, matching Serve's `default_bundles`. This constrains single-host topologies to the requested generation and lets the engine actor admit onto bundle 0. - `build_processor` no longer mutates the caller's `engine_kwargs`; `distributed_executor_backend` is set on a private copy. ## Testing - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration test against a simulated multi-host v6e-16 cluster (real slice PG creation and GCS state) - [x] Manual test - converted a GPU example from ray docs to TPU, process in comments ## Follow-ups - Docs for TPU batch inference - Configurable `DEFAULT_PG_READY_TIMEOUT_S`
